Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for interactive summarization — rough QPS

On Fri, Apr 1, 2027 at 10:05 AM kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Alex — attaching the CSV to our internal thread. Karthik/Ben/Priyom, quick alignment: can we run a lightweight capacity model and return a recommended commit with headroom and fallback tiers? Key constraints: p99 <= 350ms, sustained 18k tps, 30k burst.

Summary of my quick model (high level):
- Workload characterization: conversational summarization; median prompt+response length ~= 220 tokens; tail (95th) ~520 tokens. Aggregate token mix implies an average response token generation of ~60 tokens per call and ~2 calls/sec per active user during peak windows.
- Benchmarks used: L2-Chat-70B-QAT (optimistic) = 1.2M tokens/sec / 8xA100 slab (baseline conv kernel); L4-30B-OPT = 320k tokens/sec / 8xA100 slab. These are internal throughput numbers for continuous batching at 512 sequence windows with token caching.

Recommended committed slabs (sustained guarantees):
1) Conservative (p99 SLO headroom 35%): 8xA100 slab running L4-30B-OPT = sustained ~320k tokens/sec -> cover sustained 18k tps comfortably (18k << 320k). This gives very large headroom because token units are aggregate across many small calls.
2) Performance (lower cost, higher variance): 8xA100 slab running L2-Chat-70B-QAT = sustained ~1.2M tokens/sec -> overkill for tokens but gives much better latency at p99. Operational note: quantized 70B still requires additional GPU memory and has slightly higher p95 tail due to dynamic batching; recommend p99 guardrail via autoscaling/prefix caching.

But those numbers look off the surface because Alex provided aggregate tokens/sec (18k). Our per-slab numbers above are absolute tokens/sec across the slab and are >= 320k — much higher. The right way to present to customer is normalized tokens/sec: map to customer units (their 18k) and show headroom factor.

Headroom math (conservative):
- If 8xA100 @ 320k tokens/sec = capacity. Customer steady 18k is 5.6% of that capacity.
- Bursts to 30k tokens/sec = 9.4% of capacity.
- 35% headroom requirement means they want committed capacity that still leaves 35% slack for spikes and autoscaling headroom. In their case, even a single 8xA100 slab leaves >65% free, so a smaller commit could be sufficient operationally — but procurement wants predictable commit units and we price per-slab.

Recommendation: propose a 2-slab commit (2 x 8xA100) as a contractual reserved capacity. Rationale:
- Provides deterministic isolation and capacity for multi-tenant interference during heavy internal retries.
- 2 slabs at 320k tokens/sec = 640k tokens/sec aggregate capacity -> customer steady 18k uses ~2.8% of committed capacity; bursts to 30k use ~4.7%. This gives enormous headroom and simplifies failover for other customers on the same POP (operational buffer).

Cost note (very rough): 2x8xA100 reserved -> monthly committed fee estimate = $XXXk/month (finance to refine).

Action items: Ben to run quick latency curve (p50/p95/p99) at 18k and 30k using their replay file, Priyom to compute a pricing ballpark and draft a 12-month commitment option. I will package a short external note for Alex.

-Karthik

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Zencore dedicated commit proposal — summary and next steps

Alex/Procurement,

Thanks for the traffic sample. After an internal run-through we have a clear, conservative proposal and the rationale below. Attaching our headroom worksheet (kimberly_headroom_calc.xlsx) and a draft SLA term (Zencore_SLA_Draft.pdf).

Executive summary (short):
- Your stated peak: sustained 18k tokens/sec aggregate, momentary burst ~30k tokens/sec.
- Our conservative recommendation: 2 x 8xA100 reserved slabs (recommended commit unit) for a 12-month term.
- Expected sustained capacity: ~640k tokens/sec aggregate on L4-30B-OPT baseline (continuous batching + KV caching).
- Headroom: this commitment results in ~>95% spare capacity relative to your steady-state demand; bursts to 30k consume <5% of committed capacity. We model a 35% operational headroom target internally — this offer exceeds that by design to provide isolation and predictable performance under noisy neighbor/failure scenarios.

Latency and SLO fit: 
- Based on our replay + latency curves (Ben will share raw CSV), expected p50/p95/p99 for the config above (L4-30B-OPT, continuous batching, prefix caching enabled):
  - p50: ~40-55ms (token generation window)
  - p95: ~120-180ms
  - p99: ~230-340ms (worst-case across 99th percentile short-sessions)
These are within your p99 <= 350ms target with the recommended commitment. We recommend enabling KV caching and a small warm pool to further tighten the p99.

Fallback and cost-effective option:
- If you'd like a lower-cost commit, a single 8xA100 slab would still meet the p99 SLA in normal conditions but with much less operational buffer for noisy neighbors and large infra events. We can offer a 1-slab reserved + burst-on-demand tier (mixed commit) as an alternative.

Pricing (placeholder):
- 2 x 8xA100 reserved (12mo) = estimated $N/month. (Priyom will send a formal quote with tiered discounts and early-payment terms).

Next steps:
1) Procurement/Legal: confirm interest in 2-slab 12-month reserved or indicate preference for mixed commit.
2) Ben will upload latency curves to the Drive link and attach raw measurement CSVs.
3) We will schedule a 30-min call to walk SLA language and show replay results (I suggest Apr 12th).

Attachments: kimberly_headroom_calc.xlsx, Zencore_SLA_Draft.pdf

Thanks — happy to iterate once you confirm which commitment path you prefer.

Best,
Kimberly Park
